source: Source: Salem Witch Museum; Encyclopaedia Britannica · HAL-003

beats.html:
Nobody was burned
at Salem.

20 people were executed
in 1692. 19 were hanged.

The last one, Giles Corey,
was pressed to death
under stones.

The fire is the part
everyone remembers.
It never happened.

Ask what else you know
only because somebody
made it sound better.

Somebody you know still says burned.
You can fix that now.

label: Gentle Muse · Spooky Season
source: Source: US Patent 3335, life preserving coffin, 1843 · HAL-005

beats.html:
The Victorians were so
afraid of being buried
alive they patented
a way out.

Bells. Ropes.
Breathing tubes.

Christian Eisenbrandt
got a US patent
in 1843.

Nobody would say the
fear out loud. So they
built it instead.

Fear doesn't stay quiet.
It finds somewhere
else to go.

Somebody you know is building
something they won't name.
This one is about them.

label: Gentle Muse · Spooky Season

beats.html:
The witch trials
were not medieval.

They peaked in the 16th
and 17th centuries.

The worst of it ran
alongside the printing
press and the start of
modern science.

Progress and panic
were happening in
the same rooms.
They usually are.

Somebody you know thinks
we've moved past it.
This is the part they're missing.

label: Gentle Muse · Spooky Season
source: Source: University of Arizona excavation at Lugnano in Teverina · HAL-018

beats.html:
Archaeologists found a
child's grave with a
stone placed in
the mouth.
Roman era, in Italy.

One of several burials
meant to keep the dead
from coming back.

They couldn't argue
with the fear. So they
did something
physical about it.

We still do. Ours
is just quieter.

Somebody you know leaves
a light on.
They already knew this one.
